artifacts.title: Ehrlich v. North Georgia
artifacts.synopsis: Complaint of Devin and Tracey Ehrlich against North Georgia Presbytery regarding the Presbytery's denial of the Ehrlichs' complaint about the Intown Community Church Session's instruction prohibiting distribution of an open letter criticizing a pastor under investigation. The SJC held that the Session acted within its authority in preventing distribution of the letter, as it would disturb the peace of the church after the Presbytery had investigated and dismissed the underlying allegations against the pastor.

artifacts.synopsis: Appeal of TE Michael Chastain v. Heritage Presbytery. Chastain challenged Heritage Presbytery's judgment of guilty on charges of divisive behavior and censure of indefinite suspension from office and sacraments. The SJC sustained Presbytery's judgment, finding that Chastain's public letters to the congregation expressing disagreement with Session decisions violated his ordination vows to be subject to his brethren and maintain the peace and unity of the Church, even though his underlying views were not sinful.

artifacts.title: Chastain v. Heritage Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: TE Michael Chastain appealed his conviction and indefinite suspension by Heritage Presbytery for divisive behavior, arising from his public letters to his congregation disagreeing with Session actions regarding an associate pastor call and a related Christian school controversy. The SJC denied the appeal (20-1), upholding the conviction and censure while finding procedural errors that did not rise to reversible level; a dissent by RE Frederick Neikirk argued the charge of 'divisive behavior' failed BCO 29-1's requirement that offenses be proven from Scripture.

artifacts.synopsis: Case 93-10B arose from Southwest Presbytery's action at its June 14, 1994 meeting declaring TE Clark's suspension 'still binding' notwithstanding his appeal. The SJC held the issue moot in light of its judgment in Case 93-10 remanding the entire matter to the Presbytery for retrial.
